This code is written as a .Rmd file because it contains both R and Python chunks. (See {r} or {python} at the top of each chunk.)

It is recommended to clear your environment before running this code, as the files can be extremely large. 
Also, note that changes in the supporting packages may cause issues with the data pulls from the source.

These are the main sections of this file.

0.  Setup
1.  Download Data Using Sunpy
2.  Clean data
3.  Export Data

```{python}
# This function pulls data from the source for a given start time, end time, and with a given filepath that has
# already been created.

# Do not use this carelessly as the files can be enormous. Use the one record flag option first.

def download_data(start_time, end_time, filepath, password, one_record_flag = 1):
   # Pull data
   results = Fido.search(a.Time(start_time, end_time),a.Instrument.aia, a.Wavelength(193*u.angstrom))
   # Print the results
   print(results.show)
   # Print a warning
   print("WARNING: Please carefully review the results above. You will be downloading them to the filepath you specified in the function. Large downloads can be dangerous. If the password is not correct, then the download will not begin")
   # users_choice = input("WARNING: Please carefully review the results above. You will be downloading them to the filepath you specified in the function. Type YES to download, knowing that such large downloads can be dangerous.")
   # Return the user choice
   if (password == "YES_I_UNDERSTAND"):
     print("You have entered the correct password of " + password + ". Your download will begin shortly to location " + filepath)
     # Compute the full filepath
     full_filepath = filepath + '{file}'
     # Begin the download
     if (one_record_flag == 1):
       print("You are downloading one file.")
       downloaded_files = Fido.fetch(results[0, 0], path=full_filepath)
     else:
       print("WARNING: You are downloading all files specified above!")
       downloaded_files = Fido.fetch(results, path=full_filepath)
     # downloaded_files = Fido.fetch(results, path=full_filepath)  
   else:
     print("You have entered the incorrect password of " + password + ". The download will not begin.")
```

## Checklists

### Checklist - 2011

```{python}
# Solar Object Locator: SOL2011-04-30T21-45-49L061C108
# Find the exact location - L 61 (longitude), C 108 (latitude)
# Find the exact time - 21:45:49
# Download the data - Done
# Use the frame nearest to this without going past it and build a box around this
# For simplicity, assume it doesn't change much over the hour
# Assuming a rotation of 27.2753 days, and we have an hour of data,
# the sun will rotate 0.001528 or about 0.15%
```

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import astropy.units as u
from astropy.coordinates import SkyCoord

import sunpy.data.sample
import sunpy.map

import numpy as np

import os
```

## Checks before cutting - 2011

### Whole Plot - 2011

```{python}
# Solar Object Locator SOL2011-04-30T21-45-49L061C108

# Establish the reference coordinates and obstime
lon_2011 = 61
colat_2011 = 108
obstime_2011 = "2011/04/30T21:45:49"
image_ref_2011 = "/Users/stevenmoen/Fetch_20110430_AIA_193_Pull/aia_lev1_193a_2011_04_30t21_45_43_84z_image_lev1.fits"

# Load in the filepath - this is the last image before the flare based on the solar object locator
ref_image_2011 = sunpy.map.Map(image_ref_2011)


# Feed these into the SkyCoord system. Note that the co-latitude was established from empirical verification
ref_point_2011 = SkyCoord(lon = lon_2011*u.deg, lat = (90-colat_2011)*u.deg, frame="heliographic_carrington", observer="earth", obstime=obstime_2011)

# Plot the image
amap_2011 = sunpy.map.Map(ref_image_2011)  
amap_2011.coordinate_frame 
fig_2011 = plt.figure()
ax_2011 = plt.subplot(projection=amap_2011)  
amap_2011.plot()  
ax_2011.plot_coord(ref_point_2011, 'o')  
plt.show()
```

### Subplot - 2011

```{python}
lon_add_2011 = 8
lat_add_2011 = 4

# Add 20 to longitude and add 10 to the latitude for the top right
top_right_2011 = SkyCoord(lon = (lon_2011+lon_add_2011)*u.deg, lat = (90-colat_2011+lat_add_2011)*u.deg, frame="heliographic_carrington", observer="earth", obstime=obstime_2011)

# Establish bottom-left coordinates
bottom_left_2011 = SkyCoord(lon = (lon_2011-lon_add_2011)*u.deg, lat = (90-colat_2011-lat_add_2011)*u.deg, frame="heliographic_carrington", observer="earth", obstime=obstime_2011)

# Subset the image
ref_image_sub_2011 = ref_image_2011.submap(bottom_left = bottom_left_2011, top_right=top_right_2011)

# Plot stuff
fig_sub_2011 = plt.figure()
ax_2011 = fig_sub_2011.add_subplot(projection=ref_image_sub_2011)
image_2011 = ref_image_sub_2011.plot(axes=ax_2011)
ref_image_sub_2011.draw_limb(axes=ax_2011)
ref_image_sub_2011.draw_grid(axes=ax_2011)

# Make some room and put the title at the top of the figure
ax_2011.set_position([0.1, 0.1, 0.8, 0.7])
ax_2011.set_title(ax_2011.get_title(), pad=45)

plt.show()

# Extract the array
da_2011 = ref_image_sub_2011.data # This extracts the array
da_2011.shape # This gives us dimensions
```

## Write function to pull and subset data

```{python}
def subset_data(ref_c_lon, ref_c_lat, lon_add, lat_add, ref_time, image_path, plot_whole_flag = 0, plot_sub_flag = 0):
  # Load in the filepath - this is the last image before the flare
  ref_image = sunpy.map.Map(image_path)
  # Plot the data, if plot_whole_flag is enabled
  ref_point = SkyCoord(lon = ref_c_lon*u.deg, lat = (90-ref_c_lat)*u.deg, frame="heliographic_carrington", observer="earth", obstime=ref_time)
  # Set up the plot
  # Uncomment this
  # amap = sunpy.map.Map(ref_image)  
  # amap.coordinate_frame 
  # fig = plt.figure()
  # ax = plt.subplot(projection=amap)  
  # amap.plot()  
  # ax.plot_coord(ref_point, 'o')  
  
  # plt.show()
  # Plot the image
  # if(plot_whole_flag = 1):
  
  # plt.show()
  # This is the upper right of the box
  top_right = SkyCoord(lon = (ref_c_lon+lon_add)*u.deg, lat = (90-ref_c_lat+lat_add)*u.deg, frame="heliographic_carrington", observer="earth", obstime=ref_time)
  # This is the lower left side of the box
  bottom_left = SkyCoord(lon = (ref_c_lon-lon_add)*u.deg, lat = (90-ref_c_lat-lat_add)*u.deg, frame="heliographic_carrington", observer="earth", obstime=ref_time)
  # Subset the image
  ref_image_sub = ref_image.submap(bottom_left, top_right=top_right)
```

## Write a function to find the minimum and maximum number of rows and columns in each of the images

```{python}
def find_dimensions(image_location, ref_c_lon, ref_c_lat, lon_add, lat_add, ref_time):
  # Extract the list of all images
  image_list = sorted(os.listdir(image_location))
  # Print a test 
  # print("You have now extracted the image list")
  # Remove the .DS store  - may not be required!
  image_list.remove(".DS_Store")
  # Remove the .spikes.fits files - may not be required!
  image_list = [f for f in image_list if not f.endswith(".spikes.fits")]
  # Print the length of the list
  length_list = len(image_list)
  print("These are the number of images in the list")
  print(length_list)
  # Define a counter variable
  i = 0
  # Initialize a list
  sto_list = list()
  # Run the previous function 
  for x in range(length_list):
    # Pull the data
    da = subset_data(ref_c_lon = ref_c_lon, ref_c_lat = ref_c_lat, lon_add = lon_add, lat_add = lat_add, ref_time = ref_time, image_path = image_location + image_list[i])
    # Extract the shape
    shape_da = da.shape
    # print(shape_da)
    # Convert to a list
    shape_list = list(shape_da)
    # Append the list
    sto_list.append(shape_list)
    # Print the list 
    # print(shape_list)
    # Update the count
    i = i + 1
  # Compute the min and the max
  shape_array = np.array(sto_list, dtype='float32')
  # Find min and max of each column
  mins = np.amin(shape_array, axis=0)
  maxes = np.amax(shape_array, axis=0)
  # Print the mins and maxes
  print("This is the minimum number of rows and the minimum number of columns in the images. They may not correspond to the same image.")
  print(mins)
  print("This is the maximum number of rows and the maximum number of columns in the images. They may not correspond to the same image.")
  print(maxes)
  # print("Success")
  # Return sto_mat
  # return(sto_mat)
  return(shape_array)
```

## Write function to call the above many times

```{python}
# Description: This function feeds in .fits images and subsets them around the location (in Carrington coordinates) 
# specified in the  solar object locator. It stacks the data into an array that can be fed into the R pre-processing code

def pull_all_data(image_location, ref_c_lon, ref_c_lat, lon_add, lat_add, ref_time, rows_per_image, cols_per_image, row_buffer = 0, col_buffer = 0):
  # Extract the list of all images
  image_list = sorted(os.listdir(image_location))
  # Remove the .DS store  - may not be required!
  image_list.remove(".DS_Store")
  # Remove the .spikes.fits files - may not be required!
  image_list = [f for f in image_list if not f.endswith(".spikes.fits")]
  # Print the length of the list
  length_list = len(image_list)
  print("These are the number of images in the list")
  print(length_list)
  # Define a counter variable
  i = 0
  # Initialize a storage matrix
  # sto_mat = np.zeros((rows_per_image*length_list, cols_per_image))
  # Have the storage mat contain -999 to identify problems
  sto_mat = np.full((rows_per_image*length_list, cols_per_image), -999.)
  # np.full((239*300,302), -999.)
  # Run the previous function 
  for x in range(length_list):
    # Combine the variables
    # image_list[i]
    # print(image_list[i])
    # full_path = image_location + image_list[i]
    # print(full_path)
    # Update the storage matrix
    # sto_mat[((rows_per_image)*i):((rows_per_image)*(i+1)), 0:(cols_per_image)] = subset_data(ref_c_lon = ref_c_lon, ref_c_lat = ref_c_lat, lon_add = lon_add, lat_add = lat_add, ref_time = ref_time, image_path = image_location + image_list[i])
    # Pull the data
    da = subset_data(ref_c_lon = ref_c_lon, ref_c_lat = ref_c_lat, lon_add = lon_add, lat_add = lat_add, ref_time = ref_time, image_path = image_location + image_list[i])
    # Slide the data
    sto_mat[((rows_per_image)*i):((rows_per_image)*(i+1)), 0:(cols_per_image)] = da[0:(rows_per_image), 0:(cols_per_image)]
    # Slice the data
    # da = subset_data(ref_c_lon = ref_c_lon, ref_c_lat = ref_c_lat, lon_add = lon_add, lat_add = lat_add, ref_time = ref_time, image_path = image_location + image_list[i])
    # Print the shape of the data
    # print(da.shape)
    i = i + 1
  print("Success")
  # Return sto_mat
  return(sto_mat)

```
